feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: The latest health and science news. Updates on medicine, healthy living, nutrition, drugs, diet, and advances in science and technology. Subscribe to the Health & Science podcast.

entry.title: Gut microbes followed migrating humans across continents, new study suggests
entry.summary: New research looks at the surprising similarities in the gut microbiomes of hunter-gathers in Tanzania and horticulturalists in Bolivia, and asks: What role do these bacteria play in human health?

entry.title: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry
entry.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry Wednesday for their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

entry.title: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics has gone to a neutrino detector in Antarctica
entry.summary: The Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin Madison, who built an observatory under Antarctica.

entry.title: Vietnamese police arrest 12 suspected of prowling city streets at night, snatching cats for meat
entry.summary: State media cited investigators who said the network recruited people to ride motorcycles through neighborhoods at night, trapping up to 10 cats a night.

entry.title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in physics for work on high-energy neutrinos from space
entry.summary: The 82-year-old scientist, originally from Belgium, is affiliated with the University of Wisconsin–Madison. His research into capturing neutrinos at the South Pole dates back to the 1980s.

entry.title: Wildfire smoke affects animals in unique ways. Scientists are trying to understand it
entry.summary: The new field of "smoke ecology" examines how wildfire smoke perturbs wild places and animals — and what might be done to prevent its worst mayhem.

entry.title: Nobel medicine prize goes to 3 scientists for research into brain activity
entry.summary: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.

entry.title: Just short of its 200th birthday, a landmark natural history museum shuts down
entry.summary: Beloved for its dinosaurs, Philadelphia's storied Academy of Natural Sciences closed down this week, amid an intense fight by local residents, politicians and scientists to save it.

entry.title: This week in science: Loud birds, eating with company, and asteroid samples
entry.summary: NPR's Short Wave podcast talks about really loud birds, the benefits of eating with company and what asteroid samples could tell us about the early Earth.

entry.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
entry.summary: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.
